title: Adobe Before Q3 Earnings: Should You Hold or Fold the ADBE Stock?
author: Na
description: Adobe is set to report Q3 FY2026 results on September 10 with expected revenues of $6.67-$6.72 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $6.05-$6.10. The company's AI initiatives including Firefly, Acrobat AI Assistant, and GenStudio are driving growth with AI-first ARR exceeding $500 million. However, intensifying GenAI competition, rising investments, and near-term ARR pressure from freemium strategy expansion present concerns. Adobe shares have underperformed the sector by 23.8% year-to-date but trade at a valuation discount.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Adobe demonstrates strong AI monetization momentum with Firefly ARR approaching $300 million and AI-first ARR exceeding $500 million, plus robust enterprise adoption. However, this is offset by intensifying GenAI competition, rising investments pressuring profitability, and near-term ARR headwinds from aggressive freemium expansion. The stock's 23.8% YTD underperformance and Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating reflect these offsetting factors.

title: Adobe's Next Earnings Report on Sept. 10 Could Send the Stock Plunging. Here's Why.
author: Patrick Sanders
description: Adobe faces a critical earnings report on Sept. 10 as it navigates AI disruption to its core creative software business. The company has tripled AI-first revenue to $500 million annualized recurring revenue but must balance aggressive user acquisition through freemium offerings with meaningful monetization. Adobe stock is down 26% year-to-date amid competition from AI tools and rivals like Figma and Canva, while the company undergoes leadership transitions with a new CEO taking over in December.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock down 26% year-to-date heading into earnings. Author expects stock to slip after Sept. 10 report due to market's 'show-me' mentality. Company faces pressure to monetize AI products while managing user acquisition, and is undergoing major C-suite transitions. Competitors like Figma and Canva are gaining market share.
Mentioned as a competitive threat to Adobe with estimated 13 million users, particularly outside the U.S., potentially capturing market share from Adobe's traditional customer base.

title: Adobe Has Handed Over the CEO Job Once in 19 Years. Here's What the Stock Did After the Last Time.
author: Daniel Sparks
description: Adobe announced that Anil Chakravarthy will become CEO on December 1, 2026, replacing Shantanu Narayen who will move to executive chair. This marks only the second CEO transition in 19 years. While the stock fell 6.7% on the announcement, the article argues that current conditions favor the new CEO more than the 2007 transition did, when the Great Recession caused a 50% stock decline within 12 months. The company now has stronger recurring revenue and a more stable business model than it did in 2007.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the stock declined 6.7% on the CEO transition announcement, the article presents a balanced view. The author notes that current conditions are more favorable than the 2007 transition (stronger recurring revenue model, better valuation at 9.5x forward earnings vs 26x in 2007), and concludes 'I wouldn't sell Adobe over this transition. If anything, at this price, I'd rather buy than sell.' However, concerns remain about AI disruption and executive departures, preventing a positive rating.

title: Is Adobe's Stock Heading for $300?
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: Adobe's stock has fallen 24% year-to-date due to AI-related concerns, as AI chatbots threaten its core image creation software business. However, the stock has been rallying recently and trades at a discount (15x trailing earnings vs. S&P 500 average of 24x). Despite valid risks from potential demand erosion, the author believes Adobe's continued solid growth (11% revenue increase) and attractive valuation provide sufficient margin of safety for the stock to potentially finish the year above $300.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite significant AI-related headwinds and a 24% year-to-date decline, Adobe trades at an attractive valuation discount (15x trailing earnings) compared to the broader market. The company continues to show solid revenue growth (11%) and is incorporating AI into its products. The author believes the stock has more upside than downside at current levels and could reach $300 by year-end.
